title: Apex geo-commit controls and compliance evidence stream
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Provide a user-facing and operator-grade mechanism that lets tenants declare a deterministic geo-commit for hosted API traffic (a pinset), enforce route-level residency constraints, and produce signed, time-bounded evidence bundles suitable for audits. This work covers: API surface for pinset creation and lifecycle (create/update/retire), runtime enforcement and soft-fallback policies when capacity constraints occur, retention controls for persisted request traces and evidence artifacts, and an automated evidence stream that packages compliance artifacts on a schedule or on-demand.
acceptance_criteria: Console: Tenant can create a geo-commit pinset with prioritized regions and an optional soft-fallback policy via the Residency page.
API: CRUD endpoints exist for pinsets and return deterministic routing metadata used by the runtime.
Runtime: Requests for pinned tenants are routed to preferred regions when capacity available; soft-fallbacks follow configured policy (secondary regions, burst pool, or failover) and are logged.

Evidence: The system generates a signed evidence bundle containing route decisions, retention profile, request digests (hashed), and region attestations; bundles are exportable via API and stored for configured retention.
Retention: Admin can set per-tenant retention profiles that control how long raw traces vs digest records are kept; enforcement hooks prevent premature deletion while evidence references exist.
SLOs: Pin-enforced requests maintain SLA tiers; when soft-fallback used, the console surfaces degraded-residency alerts and ticket suggestions.
Security: Evidence bundles are signed with customer-scoped keys and include an immutable manifest; change history for pinsets is auditable in the console.
Tests: End-to-end integration tests validate routing under capacity pressure, evidence bundle integrity, and retention lifecycle transitions.
implementation_notes: Design: Pinset model includes: id, tenant_id, ordered_regions, fallback_policy (ALLOW_SECONDARY|BURST_POOL|FAIL), retention_profile_id, created_by, created_at, retired_at
Runtime: Routing layer should consult pinset cache with TTL and fallback to control-plane on cache miss; prefer deterministic hashing across hosts to reduce route churn

Fallback trade-off: ALLOW_SECONDARY keeps availability but expands data footprint; BURST_POOL reduces geographic diffusion but may increase latency. Default to ALLOW_SECONDARY with opt-in for strict residency.

Evidence packaging: Produce ZIP containing manifest.json (signed), route_log.csv (hashed request ids), retention_profile.yml, certs/region_attestations.pem; sign with KMS key scoped to the tenant's residency namespace.
Retention enforcement: Introduce evidence-anchored retention hold so evidence bundles reference digests and prevent raw trace deletion until retention TTL or manual purge is executed.
Console UX: Add Residency -> Pinsets list, create flow with region chooser and fallback radio group; show recent fallback events and a link to download latest evidence bundle.
API: Add endpoints POST /v1/tenants/:id/pinsets, GET /v1/tenants/:id/pinsets/:pinset_id, PATCH, DELETE (soft-delete). Add evidence endpoint GET /v1/tenants/:id/pinsets/:id/evidence?since=YYYY-MM-DD
Observability: Emit metric residency.pinset.enforced, residency.pinset.fallback.{policy}, residency.evidence.generated and a trace span residency.evidence.create
Security: Coordinate with security to use tenant-scoped KMS keys (ENG-19320) and obtain review before enabling signed bundles by default.
